answer: The protocol enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes achieve consensus while 1,000 fakes stall, failing to hold the ember of valid state. A verifier challenges agents by requesting random data indices; failure to return data matching the inlet of the working set triggers an immediate penalty. This ledge of latency ensures each agent keeps unique bus access. Honest participants pay 120 watts to maintain their status, while 1,000 fakes incur 120,000 watts, rendering mass-identity farms infeasible and ensuring security.
